newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended slightly lower on Monday from the previous New York close after two-way trade during a relatively quiet day, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$358.50/359.00 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$358.80/359.30 close on Friday.
Australian professionals were said to be selling gold to establish short positions which pushed the market down below New York's finish, traders said.
But intra-day trade saw buying from Japanese traders on a drop of the dollar/yen, they said.
Some professionals were also shortcovering, bullion dealers said.
Dealers said $360 per ounce offered strong resistence, and expected gold to trade within a narrow range. They saw the market testing generally higher, but no spectacular breakthroughs were expected.
Local gold ended HK$3 lower at HK$3,313 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at nil.
